summary: The 2026-08-29 fixes worked — the port now runs indefinitely (1200 frames, no runtime error) and animates a noise field that is spatially almost the SAME field as the original's (cross-side spatial correlation 0.69-0.96 at matched dials) — but its heat/colour mapping is ~4-5x too cold (blue channel is 0 everywhere, max R 167 vs the original's 255, mean brightness 10 vs 47), a quarter of the Mode dial (0.25-0.50) renders PURE BLACK on the port, Mode is still quantized as floor(v*4) with two byte-identical bands against the original's round(v*3) four distinct modes, and the untouched defaults differ (orig Mode index 1 / RisingSpeed 0.60 / MorphSpeed 0.60 / Scale 0.20 vs port Mode index 0 / RisingSpeed ~0.10 / MorphSpeed 0.10 / Scale ~0.22).
observations: CRASH IS FIXED. rj-leak-s60-f20 (1200 frames @20 fps, absolute frames 0-1199, i.e. well past the old frame-512 failure) reports runtimeError null on BOTH sides. The port's meanBrightness is still changing at frame 1181 and its motion series sums 196 over frames 0-499 and 200 over frames 500-1199 — it keeps working at the same rate for the whole run. rj-late (--skip 200 --seconds 10) is likewise healthy: port meanBrightness avg 10.1, motionLit avg 0.5, no error. Every other run in this judgement (including a 240 s survey and 20 s dialed runs) was error-free too.

THE PORT IS NOT FROZEN, it is dim and slow. At untouched defaults its `motion` reads 0.3-0.4 with zeroMotionFrames 68/120 (baseline) and 181/200 (late window), but `motionLit` is 0.5-0.6 and a --dump at widening lags shows real movement: whole-frame correlation of frame(t) with frame(t+dt) falls 0.998 -> 0.994 -> 0.985 -> 0.969 -> 0.902 -> 0.784 -> 0.648 over dt = 0.05/0.1/0.15/0.2/0.3/0.4/0.5 s (48x48). The low motion stat is the classic dim+slow false freeze.

HEADLINE COLOUR GAP (unchanged from the prior verdict, and now the dominant defect). Untouched baseline 16x16: orig meanBrightness 46.4, meanRGB (76.4, 45.2, 17.5); port meanBrightness 9.8, meanRGB (26.1, 3.2, 0.0). The port's BLUE CHANNEL IS EXACTLY 0 in every single run of this judgement (baseline, 60 s, 240 s, every mode, every dial setting) while the original's meanB averages 17.5 with max 32 — the port never reaches the white-hot top of the fire ramp at all.

Pixel-value distributions over 4 dumped frames (16x16 = 1024 px each). Untouched: orig luminance p50/p75/p90/p99/max = 21/65/127/255/255, max RGB (255,255,255), 89% lit; port 3/14/30/63/92, max RGB (167,110,0), 78% lit. sliderMode=0.1 (both sides in their mode/band 0): orig 17/42/85/255/255 vs port 3/14/30/63/92. sliderMode=0.9: orig 7/27/62/255/255 vs port 0/5/17/47/65. The port sits at roughly 0.2-0.35x the original at every quantile and its ceiling is capped around R=167.

THE PALETTE CURVE ITSELF IS ROUGHLY RIGHT, THE HEAT DRIVING IT IS NOT. Binning dumped pixels by R and reading mean G/B (untouched): orig R64-95 -> G14 B0, R96-127 -> G45 B0, R128-159 -> G88 B0, R160-191 -> G142 B0, R192-223 -> G202 B24, R224-255 -> G249 B224. Port: R64-95 -> G10 B0, R96-127 -> G27 B0, R128-159 -> G65 B0, R160-191 -> G108 B0, and NOTHING above R191. So the port's ramp is the same black->red->orange->yellow family but runs ~20-25% cooler in G at equal R, and simply never populates the two hot bins where the original turns white (the original puts 7% of its pixels in R224-255 with B~224).

NOISE FIELD AND SPATIAL PHASE ARE EXCELLENT. Frame-by-frame cross-side spatial correlation of luminance (mean-subtracted, whole grid) at sliderMode=0.1: 0.711 / 0.846 / 0.959 / 0.815 at t = 0.5/1.5/2.5/3.5 s. Fully dialed match (Mode 0.1, Scale 0.2, Rising 0.6, Morph 0.6): 0.761 / 0.673 / 0.861 / 0.734 / 0.793 at t = 1..5 s. The contact sheets confirm it visually — at t=0 both sides draw the same 'C'-shaped blob in the top-left of a 16x16 grid. The port is drawing the SAME field with the SAME phase; it is the colour mapping and the dial defaults that are wrong.

Rig envelope matches: both sides' 60 s rhythm images show the same static column envelope (bright centre column, dark left/right edges) with no regime structure. Feature size also matches — spatial half-correlation width at 48x48 with dials matched: Scale 0 orig 11.6 px / port 11.2 px; Scale 0.5 orig 6.5 / port 8.8; Scale 1 orig 8.1 / port 7.6.

NEITHER SIDE IS FRAME-RATE COUPLED. Vertical drift measured by whole-frame correlation at 48x48 (time-mean profile subtracted, symmetric +/-30-row lag scan) at 10 / 20 / 40 fps: orig -50 / -50 / -50 rows/s at 0.1 s lag and -55 / -50 / -50 at 0.2 s; port -10 / -10 / -10 and -20 / -20 / -20. Both are time-based.

RISE SPEED AT UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS: orig ~-50 to -53 rows/s at 48x48 (-20 rows/s at 16x16, i.e. ~1.1-1.25 grid-heights/s); port ~-20 rows/s at 48x48 (-7 to -8 at 16x16, ~0.45 heights/s). The port is ~2.5x TOO SLOW out of the box — the opposite direction from the prior verdict. The cause is the default value, not the law: see the next observation.

RISE SPEED AT MATCHED DIALS is ~2x TOO FAST. With Mode 0.1, Scale 0.2, RisingSpeed 0.6, MorphSpeed 0.6 set identically on both sides (48x48): orig -60/-70/-80/-80 rows/s at lags 0.05/0.1/0.15/0.2 s; port -140/-140/-140/-140 rows/s at the same lags. So the port's RisingSpeed law is roughly 1.8-2x hot while its DEFAULT is 6x cold.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS RECOVERED BY DIAL-MATCHING (101-point 0.01-step sweep of each dial alone, frame dumped at t=0.95 s and diffed pixel-by-pixel against the untouched render). Original: sliderRisingSpeed = 0.60 EXACTLY (mean abs diff 0.00; next best 0.59 -> 9.42), sliderScale = 0.20 EXACTLY (0.00; next best 0.19 -> 6.02), sliderMorphSpeed = 0.60 EXACTLY, mode index 1. Port: sliderRisingSpeed ~= 0.100 (best diff 0.094 over a 0.005-step refinement), sliderScale ~= 0.220 (best diff 0.122), sliderMorphSpeed = 0.10 EXACTLY (diff 0.00), mode index 0. So the port's two speed dials default to 0.10 where the original's default to 0.60.

MODE QUANTIZATION STILL DIFFERS (41-value 0.025-step sweep, frame-hash clustering). Original: 4 distinct hashes with boundaries strictly between 0.150/0.175, 0.475/0.500 and 0.825/0.850 = 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 = round(v*3). Port: boundaries at 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 = floor(v*4). The two sides therefore select different modes over most of the dial (v=0.2: orig mode 1, port band 0; v=0.8: orig mode 2, port band 3).

PORT MODE BAND 1 IS COMPLETELY BLACK — a NEW/unfixed defect worth more than the quantization itself. Every port render with sliderMode in [0.25, 0.50) is all-zero: rj-portmode1-long (sliderMode=0.3, 600 frames @10 fps over 60 s) gives port meanBrightness min=max=0, motion 0, 600/600 zeroMotionFrames, runtimeError null, while the original at the same setting runs at mean 47 motion 20. It stays black under every other dial combination tried too (Mode 0.3 + Scale 0.2 + Rising 0.6 + Morph 0.6; Mode 0.4 + Scale 0.5 + Rising 1 + Morph 1; Mode 0.26 + Scale 1 + Rising 0.5 + Morph 0.5) — all port mean 0. That is 25% of the Mode dial's travel producing no light.

PORT STILL COLLAPSES TWO MODES. Its bands [0, 0.25) and [0.50, 0.75) are BYTE-IDENTICAL (hash 8204f25e at all 17 sampled values across both bands, and identical stats meanB 9.5 / motion 0.3 at v=0.1 and v=0.6). The original's modes 0 and 2 are genuinely different: same mean brightness (33.9 vs 34.0, same meanRGB 62/31/8) but mode 2 moves noticeably faster — 4 s `motion` 4.7 vs 7.0, `motionLit` 5.2 vs 8.0 — and their frame hashes differ (8cf5cd96 vs 5dd9106d). So the port has 2 non-black looks where the original has 4.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULT MODE IS STILL WRONG. The original's untouched frame hash (6bde1eb2) is byte-identical to sliderMode = 0.175..0.475, i.e. mode index 1 — the brightest, most turbulent, most white-hot of the four (meanB 44.8, motion 12.3). The port's untouched hash (8204f25e) is its band 0/2 — the dim smooth red-blob look (meanB 9.5, motion 0.3). Out of the box the two sides show different modes, and the port's own band-1 equivalent is the black one.

The original's four modes, 4 s @20 fps, all other dials untouched: mode 0 (v<1/6) meanB 33.9 motion 4.7, calm mottled amber with white cores; mode 1 (1/6..1/2, the default) meanB 44.8 motion 12.3, big fast turbulent white-hot flame; mode 2 (1/2..5/6) meanB 34.0 motion 7.0, same brightness/palette as mode 0 but flickering ~1.5x faster; mode 3 (>5/6) meanB 25.4 motion 10.0, dimmer, finer, faster. The port's: band 0/2 meanB 9.5 motion 0.3; band 1 black; band 3 meanB 4.5 motion 1.0 (coarse dark-red blobs).

Control SURFACE matches exactly: both sides expose sliderMode (slider), showNumberMode (showNumber), sliderScale (slider), sliderRisingSpeed (slider), sliderMorphSpeed (slider). No missing or invented controls. The probe calls all four sliders responsive on both sides (orig maxDelta 24.7-38.7; port 4.7-7.1 — the smaller port deltas track its 5x lower brightness, not deadness).

No regime structure on either side. 60 s @5 fps and 240 s @2 fps surveys both show a single continuous flicker regime with a static centre-bright/edge-dark column envelope; orig brightnessTrend steady (meanB 47, min 28 max 60), port steady (meanB 9.7, min 5 max 14). Nothing long-period was missed.
Seed-insensitive on both sides: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give orig mean 46 motion 12 and port mean 10 motion 0 identically. No one-seed fluke.

dials.name: sliderMode
dials.origEffect: 4 distinct modes selected by round(v*3), boundaries measured at 1/6, 1/2, 5/6. Mode 0: calm mottled amber fire with white cores (meanB 33.9, 4 s motion 4.7). Mode 1 (the untouched default): large fast turbulent white-hot flame (meanB 44.8, motion 12.3). Mode 2: same brightness and palette as mode 0 but ~1.5x faster flicker (meanB 34.0, motion 7.0). Mode 3: dimmer, finer-grained, fast (meanB 25.4, motion 10.0). Every mode reaches RGB (255,255,255).
dials.portEffect: 4 bands selected by floor(v*4), boundaries at 0.25/0.50/0.75 — misaligned with the original's. Band 0 [0,0.25) and band 2 [0.50,0.75) are BYTE-IDENTICAL (dim smooth dark-red blobs, meanB 9.5, motion 0.3) and band 0 is also the untouched default. Band 1 [0.25,0.50) renders PURE BLACK for 60 s under every dial combination tested. Band 3 [0.75,1] is a very dark coarse red blob field (meanB 4.5). So 2 usable looks vs the original's 4, one quarter of the dial dead, and neither look reaches white.

dials.name: sliderScale
dials.origEffect: Blob size plus a strong inverse speed effect. Spatial half-correlation width at 48x48 (other dials pinned Mode 0.1 / Rising 0.6 / Morph 0.6): 11.6 px at v=0, 6.5 px at 0.5, 8.1 px at 1. Rise speed falls hard with v: about -110 rows/s at 0, -25 to -30 at 0.5, -20 at 1. Untouched default value recovered as exactly 0.20.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and near-identical feature-size trend (11.2 / 8.8 / 7.6 px at v = 0 / 0.5 / 1), but every speed is ~2-4x the original's (-75 rows/s at 0.5, -40 at 1; at v=0 the port's per-frame shift exceeds a +/-30-row lag scan at 0.05 s spacing, i.e. faster than ~600 rows/s, and aliases). Untouched default recovered as ~0.22, essentially the original's 0.20. Brightness flat at meanB ~9.5 across the sweep (orig ~34) — the cold-palette bug applies at every Scale.

dials.name: sliderRisingSpeed
dials.origEffect: Monotonic, strongly convex rise-speed curve. Measured at 48x48 with Mode 0.1, Scale 0.5, Morph 0: v=0 -> ~-10 rows/s, 0.2 -> -10 to -20, 0.4 -> -20 to -25, 0.6 -> -30, 0.8 -> -60, 1.0 -> -120 rows/s. Untouched default is exactly 0.60.
dials.portEffect: Same monotonic direction and a similar convex shape, but roughly 2x hot at every value: v=0 -> ~-10 rows/s, 0.2 -> -20 to -25, 0.4 -> -40 to -45, 0.6 -> -70 to -80, 0.8 -> -120, 1.0 -> -190 to -200. Untouched default is ~0.10 instead of the original's 0.60, so the out-of-the-box fire creeps at ~-20 rows/s where the original's climbs at ~-50.

dials.name: sliderMorphSpeed
dials.origEffect: Controls how fast the field reshapes in place. With RisingSpeed pinned to 0, whole-frame autocorrelation at 0.3 s lag falls 0.978 / 0.978 / 0.961 / 0.900 / 0.895 as v goes 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1, and at 0.7 s lag 0.890 / 0.892 / 0.819 / 0.830 / 0.644. Untouched default is exactly 0.60.
dials.portEffect: Same monotonic trend, slightly steeper: 0.3 s lag correlation 0.959 / 0.953 / 0.929 / 0.847 / 0.676 and 0.7 s lag 0.851 / 0.785 / 0.754 / 0.734 / 0.864 across the same values. Behaviourally the best-matching dial. Its untouched default, however, is exactly 0.10 against the original's 0.60.

dials.name: showNumberMode
dials.origEffect: Display-only readout of the mode index (0-3 via round(v*3)); not observable from rendered output.
dials.portEffect: Present with the same name and kind, but since the port derives its index as floor(v*4) the number it reports will disagree with the original's over most of the dial's travel.

feedback: CONFIRMED FIXED — do not re-open: the frame-512 'array element budget exceeded' crash is gone. The port ran 1200 frames at 20 fps, 600 frames at 10 fps over 60 s, and a 240 s survey with runtimeError null and motion still accumulating at the last frame. Everything below is about fidelity, not liveness.

FIX FIRST: sliderMode in [0.25, 0.50) renders PURE BLACK (mean 0, motion 0, 0% lit) for 60 s on the port, under every dial combination tested. That is a quarter of the Mode dial producing no light, and it is the band the original uses for its BEST-looking mode. Find why that branch emits nothing — the other three bands render fine, so it is that branch alone, not a global gate.

FIX SECOND (the dominant visual gap): the heat -> colour mapping is ~4-5x too cold. The palette CURVE is broadly right (G tracks R in the same family) but the heat value driving it never exceeds about 0.65 of full scale: the port's blue channel is EXACTLY 0 in every render of this judgement and its max R is 167 (untouched) / 160 (matched dials) / 140 (mode 3), while the original reaches (255,255,255) in all four modes and puts ~7% of its pixels in R224-255 with B~224. Targets to hit at untouched defaults on a 16x16 grid: meanBrightness ~47 with meanRGB ~(76, 45, 18) against the port's current 10 / (26, 3, 0); luminance quantiles p50/p75/p90/p99/max of 21/65/127/255/255 against the port's 3/14/30/63/92. Also nudge the ramp warmer at equal R — at R128-159 the original's mean G is 88, the port's 65; at R160-191 it is 142 vs 108.

FIX THE MODE QUANTIZATION: the original maps the slider with round(v*3) (boundaries measured at exactly 1/6, 1/2, 5/6), giving 4 modes. The port uses floor(v*4) (boundaries 0.25/0.50/0.75). Change the mapping so both the rendered mode and the showNumberMode readout agree with the original across the whole dial.

GIVE MODE 2 ITS OWN LOOK: the port's bands 0 and 2 are byte-identical at every sampled value. On the original, modes 0 and 2 share brightness and palette (both meanB ~34, meanRGB 62/31/8) but mode 2 flickers about 1.5x faster (4 s motion 7.0 vs 4.7, motionLit 8.0 vs 5.2). Implement mode 2 as a faster-flickering variant rather than aliasing it onto mode 0.

FIX THE UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS — this is cheap and highly visible. Dial-matching pins the original's untouched state exactly: sliderMode -> mode index 1, sliderScale = 0.20, sliderRisingSpeed = 0.60, sliderMorphSpeed = 0.60. The port's are: mode index 0, Scale ~0.22 (fine), RisingSpeed ~0.10, MorphSpeed 0.10. Set the port's initial mode variable to 1 and both speed defaults to 0.60. Verification recipe: sweep one dial at a time in 0.01 steps with --seconds 1 --fps 20 --dump 0.95 and diff each frame against the untouched render — the original hits mean-abs-diff exactly 0.00 at 0.60 / 0.20 / 0.60, so the port should too.

AFTER the default fix, scale the RisingSpeed LAW down by ~2x. With all four dials set identically on both sides (Mode 0.1, Scale 0.2, Rising 0.6, Morph 0.6) the original rises at -70 to -80 rows/s on a 48x48 grid and the port at -140. Target rise speeds at 48x48 with Mode 0.1 / Scale 0.5 / Morph 0: RisingSpeed 0 -> ~10 rows/s, 0.2 -> ~15, 0.4 -> ~22, 0.6 -> ~30, 0.8 -> ~60, 1.0 -> ~120. The port currently gives ~10 / 22 / 42 / 75 / 120 / 195. The curve SHAPE is already right (convex, flat until ~0.4 then accelerating); it just needs a ~2x gain reduction in the mid-range.

DO NOT TOUCH the noise generation, the spatial mapping, or the rig envelope — they are now excellent. At matched dials the two sides' luminance fields correlate spatially at 0.69-0.96 frame by frame (they draw the same blob in the same place at the same time), feature half-widths agree within ~1-2 px across the whole Scale sweep at 48x48, and both sides show the same static centre-bright / edge-dark column envelope over 240 s.

DO NOT TOUCH sliderMorphSpeed's law — it matches well (autocorrelation at 0.3 s lag of 0.959/0.953/0.929/0.847/0.676 across v = 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 against the original's 0.978/0.978/0.961/0.900/0.895, same monotonic trend, and neither side lets Morph leak into rise speed). Only its DEFAULT value (0.10 vs 0.60) is wrong.
DO NOT TOUCH the timing model: both sides are correctly time-based, with rise speed identical at 10, 20 and 40 fps on each side. No frame-rate coupling was introduced by the fix.
